AAPL.rationale: Apple presents a strong fundamental case anchored by accelerating earnings (+18.3% YoY EPS growth in Q1 FY2026, +17% revenue growth in Q2 FY2026), expanding margins (gross margin up to 48.2% in Q1, 49.3% in Q2 per CNBC), and exceptional cash generation ($53.92B OCF in Q1 alone). The franchise is durable: Services at 26%+ of revenue with 70%+ margins, an all-time-high installed base, and a capital-light AI strategy that preserves shareholder returns. The balance sheet is strengthening — debt down $6.3B YoY, equity up 32%. Valuation has compressed to 34.1x PE, in the lower third of its 30.2–43.1x 12-month range, while fundamentals are clearly improving — a favorable divergence. The Q2 FY2026 earnings beat (Apr 30) with 14–17% June-quarter guidance well above Street expectations, plus the $100B buyback authorization and abandonment of the net-cash-neutral target, constitute a credible near-term re-rating catalyst. Offsetting: oil at $108.64/bbl (+76% surge) threatens supply-chain costs and consumer demand; 10Y yields at 4.40% compress the equity risk premium; and regulatory risk to Services margins (70% probability per qualitative assessment) is material. The score of +0.35 reflects solid fundamentals and trajectory (pillar 1), fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation vs own history (pillar 2), and a modest catalyst boost from the Q2 beat and guidance raise (pillar 3), tempered by the hostile macro backdrop and regulatory overhang.
key_factors: Q1 FY2026 revenue $143.76B (+15.7% YoY), EPS $2.84 (+18.3% YoY) — accelerating growth trajectory
Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.18B (+17% YoY), EPS $2.01, Services $30.98B (+16% YoY), gross margin 49.3% — double beat with strong forward guidance of 14-17% June-quarter growth vs ~9.5% Street expectation
Gross margin expanding: 48.2% in Q1 (up from 46.9% YoY), 49.3% in Q2 — structural mix improvement toward high-margin Services
Operating cash flow $53.92B in Q1 (+80.1% YoY), $28B+ in Q2 — exceptional cash generation enabling aggressive buybacks
Balance sheet deleveraging: total debt down from $94.80B to $88.50B, equity up from $66.76B to $88.19B (+32.1%)
PE at 34.12x in lower third of 30.2–43.1x range; multiple has compressed ~7 turns from Nov 2025 peak of ~41x while earnings accelerated
$100B additional buyback authorization + 4% dividend increase + abandonment of net-cash-neutral target — major capital allocation catalyst (Apr 30, 2026)
CEO transition: Tim Cook to Executive Chairman Sep 1, 2026; John Ternus (25-year veteran) as successor — managed, low-risk continuity
Macro headwinds: WTI oil $108.64/bbl (+76%), 10Y yield 4.40%, yield curve narrowing to 0.52% — risk to consumer demand and cost structure
Regulatory risk: 70% probability of adverse App Store policy changes; could reduce Services revenue 5-15%
China risk: Greater China 15.5% of revenue ($64.4B FY2025); Q2 up 28% to $20.5B but geopolitical exposure remains material

sources_cited.excerpt: Apple delivered a strong fiscal Q2 earnings beat with $111.18B in revenue (up 17% YoY) and $2.01 EPS, exceeding expectations. The company guided for June-quarter revenue growth of 14-17%, well ahead of Street expectations of ~9%.
Services revenue in the quarter rose about 16% from $26.65 billion a year ago... Gross margin has been steadily moving up in recent years, reaching 49.3% in the latest quarter.

We are no longer providing net cash neutral as a formal target... our Board has authorized an additional $100 billion for share repurchases, and we are also raising our dividend by 4% to $0.27 per share.

Regulatory and Antitrust Pressure (Probability: 70%)... Forced changes to App Store policies could reduce Services revenue by 5-15%. China Geopolitical Risk (Probability: 60%)... Greater China represents 15.5% of revenue ($64.4B in FY2025).

Services: Comprising the App Store, Apple Pay, iCloud+, and the newly launched Apple Intelligence+, this segment now accounts for over 26% of total revenue. It boasts margins significantly higher (70%+) than the hardware business (35-40%).
North America's foldable smartphone market is expected to grow 48% YoY in 2026, with Apple set to capture a 46% share.
